data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The large service's internal redundancy is centrally controlled; the decentralized network's independence is emergent.","Internal diversity in a large service is a design choice; independence in a decentralized network is a structural property."],"overturn_conditions":["If a decentralized network survives a correlated failure without a demonstrable barrier, the necessity of the barrier is refuted.","If the large service can internally replicate the barrier, the sufficiency of decentralization is weakened."],"shared_structure":["Conditional superiority: decentralized wins only if a barrier exists.","Redundancy absorption: large service can absorb component failures up to its redundancy limit."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a firebreak stops fire spread only if it is clear of fuel, a causal independence barrier stops failure propagation only if it is truly independent.","The conditional claim transfers: without a firebreak, the building with more fire extinguishers (redundancy) is safer."]},"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure if and only if a demonstrable causal independence barrier exists between the services. Without such a barrier, the large service with strict internal redundancy is strictly more resilient because it can absorb failures of any subset of its components up to its redundancy limit.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The large service can internally replicate the causal independence barrier (e.g., by using diverse subsystems internally), matching the decentralized network's benefit while retaining more total redundancy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network's operators are independently incentivized but converge on the same technology stack, negating the barrier.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service cannot afford the operational complexity of internal diversity, making the barrier impractical to replicate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal independence barriers (e.g., different operators, different codebases, different infrastructure providers) prevent a single root cause from propagating to all services. If the barrier is absent, decentralization provides no protection against a shared cause (e.g., a shared cloud provider failure), and the large service's higher redundancy is strictly superior. The barrier is not implied by organizational separation alone; it must be demonstrated.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
